articles.title: Service Incident - August 19, 2026 - Support | Multiple Pods - App errors and timeouts
articles.body:
Summary

On August 19, 2026 from 6:27 UTC to 8:09 UTC, some Support customers using third party apps experienced errors and difficulties accessing those applications. The issue affected customers in several pods and resulted in 503 errors or timeouts.

Timeline

August 19, 2026 08:00 AM UTC | 1:00AM PT
 
We’re investigating an issue affecting third-party app functionality, where some customers may be unable to use certain apps or may encounter errors and timeouts. Our teams have observed that service is now operating normally. Please refresh your browser and check whether the issue has been resolved on your end. Thank you for your patience as we worked through this.
 
 
August 19, 2026 08:33 AM UTC | 1:33AM PT
 
We’re happy to report that the issue affecting third-party app functionality has been fully resolved and service has been restored. We appreciate your understanding and cooperation throughout this incident.

Root Cause Analysis

This incident was caused by a front-end change that unintentionally deprecated a feature flag which controlled routing for requests from applications, causing those requests to result in errors.

Resolution

To fix this issue, the feature flag was manually re-enabled, which restored application request routing to its intended path.

Remediation Items

  1. Change feature flag deprecation controls.
  2. Revisit and improve feature flag adjustment permissions.
  3. Improve runbook for similar deploys to reduce response time in similar scenarios.

FOR MORE INFORMATION

For current system status information about Zendesk and specific impacts to your account, visit our system status page. If you have additional questions about this incident, contact Zendesk customer support.

articles.name: Announcing the ability to search for custom object records in action flows
articles.title: Announcing the ability to search for custom object records in action flows
articles.body:
Zendesk is pleased to announce that it is now possible to search for relevant custom object records directly within action flows, helping AI agent and human agents alike in retrieving additional customer context that is necessary to solve tickets.

This announcement includes the following topics:

  • What is changing?
  • Why is Zendesk making this change?
  • What do I need to do?

What is changing?

Action builder has a new Zendesk action: Search for custom object records. With this new action, you can retrieve related custom object records that isn't stored directly in a ticket, user profile, or organization already referenced in the action flow and without needing to know the custom object record ID.

For example, to fetch the ticket requester's five most recent returns, you could configure a Search for custom object records action in the following manner:

  • Search for object type: Return
  • Conditional filters: (Customer = Requester) AND (Status =Completed OR Status = Denied)
  • Sort order: Created at
  • Sort by: Descending
  • Page size: 5

With this information, an AI agent or action flow could determine whether to approve the return request or escalate to a human for approval.

For more information, see Understanding the difference between looking up and searching for custom object records in action flows.

Why is Zendesk making this change?

Zendesk understands that customer context frequently lives in custom objects, such as orders, contracts, entitlements, returns, and assets. Previously, an action flow could look up a custom object record when it already had the record ID, but it couldn't easily find related records based on information already available in the workflow. This new search action makes that related context available to downstream workflow steps, helping admins build more capable and personalized automations.

What do I need to do?

The new Search for custom object records action is being rolled out to all accounts with access to action flows and custom objects. You can create or edit your action flows to include this step. See Creating action flows and  Understanding the difference between looking up and searching for custom object records in action flows.

If you have feedback or questions related to this announcement, visit our community forum where we collect and manage customer product feedback. For general assistance with your Zendesk products, contact Zendesk Customer Support.

articles.name: Understanding the difference between looking up and searching for custom object records in action flows
articles.title: Understanding the difference between looking up and searching for custom object records in action flows
articles.body:
Action flowsare user-defined automated workflows that can perform actions in Zendesk and connected external systems. Within action flows, there are two ways to retrieve custom object records: theLookup custom object recordstep and theSearch for custom object recordstep. While both return information about custom object records, it's important to understand when to use each of these actions.

What's my plan?
All Suites Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus
Support Enterprise

Summary: ◀▼

You can retrieve custom object records in action flows using two methods: lookup by record ID for specific records linked to tickets or users, and search by object type with filter conditions, search terms, and sorting options to find multiple relevant records. Use lookup when you have the record ID, and search when you need to find records based on characteristics or keywords.

Action flows are user-defined automated workflows that can perform actions in Zendesk and connected external systems. Within action flows, there are two ways to retrieve custom object records: the Lookup custom object record step and the Search for custom object record step. While both return information about custom object records, it's important to understand when to use each of these actions.

The Lookup custom object record action requires a record ID as input and returns data only about that particular record. This action is commonly used when a record is related to a ticket, user, or other object that has already come up in a previous step of the action flow and the ID can be entered as a variable from a previous step.

The Search for custom object record action takes an object type and conditions as input rather than an ID. This makes it possible to return one or more relevant custom object records based on other characteristics of the records. When configuring the search conditions for this action, you can specify the following:
  • Filter conditions: The characteristics matching records must have, in the format of Category | Operator | Value. Conditions can be nested up to three layers deep.
  • Search term: The word or phrase is searched against all text-based fields in the records. Separate multiple words with spaces.
  • Sort order: Sort the matching records by name, when it was created, or when it was last updated. If sort order isn't specified, it defaults to relevance.
  • Page size: Specify the number of records to return per page.
  • Sort by: Sort the matching records by ascending or descending order. Available only when sort order is specified.

articles.name: Setting up Contact Center on a Zendesk-managed AWS account
articles.title: Setting up Contact Center on a Zendesk-managed AWS account
articles.body:
Use this guide when setting up Zendesk Contact Center for a customer where Zendesk provisions and manages the AWS account. In this deployment model, Zendesk and Zendesk partners complete the customer-specific Amazon Connect and Zendesk configuration described below. Some steps require access that only Zendesk employees have; those steps are marked clearly.

What's my plan?
Add-on Contact Center

Summary: ◀▼

This guide helps you set up Contact Center on a Zendesk-managed AWS account, from AWS account provisioning to telephony testing. You’ll confirm federated access, create a test user, claim a test phone number, validate inbound and outbound calling, and check that call recordings and transcripts appear on tickets. It also covers optional cleanup of test resources.

Use this guide when setting up Zendesk Contact Center for a customer where Zendesk provisions and manages the AWS account. In this deployment model, Zendesk and Zendesk partners complete the customer-specific Amazon Connect and Zendesk configuration described below. Some steps require access that only Zendesk employees have; those steps are marked clearly.

Before you begin, make sure you have:

  • Administrator access to the Zendesk account and its valid subdomain, such as example.zendesk.com
  • The customer technical contact and the required AWS Region, telephony, and SSO details
  • A Zendesk contact who can provision the AWS account and perform internal Monitor or Contact Center Admin actions
  • An active Contact Center license

This article contains the following topics:

  • Step 1: Zendesk provisions the AWS account
  • Step 2: Configure Connect access and validate settings
  • Step 3: Test telephony capabilities
  • Step 4: Clean up (Optional)

Related articles:

  • About AWS services in Contact Center
  • Accessing Amazon Connect and AWS Console from Contact Center

Step 1: Zendesk provisions the AWS account

Important: The actions in this step require a Zendesk employee with access to the relevant internal provisioning and administration systems.

Start by providing the following information to your Zendesk contact:

  • Zendesk account name, ID, and valid subdomain, such as example.zendesk.com
  • Customer technical contact details
  • Intended Amazon Connect Region
  • Required telephony and SSO configuration details
  • Preferred Amazon Connect instance name

Your Zendesk contact will provision or associate the AWS account, create or identify the Amazon Connect instance, complete the required internal account and SKU-linking steps, and confirm when the account is ready.

Step 2: Configure Connect access and validate settings

In this section, you'll configure a test user, claim a test phone number, and optionally enable outbound dialing in your Amazon Connect instance.

2.1 Configure test user

After Zendesk confirms that the AWS account and Amazon Connect instance are ready, create a test user so you can validate agent access.

To configure a test user

  1. Navigate to the Overview page and click the Log in for emergency access link:

  2. From the Amazon Connect Dashboard, navigate to User Management and click Add new users:

  3. From the Add user page:

    • Enter the First name.

    • Enter the Last name.

    • Enter the Login. This must match the corresponding Zendesk user's primary email address exactly, including capitalization.

    • Select the Security profile permissions, such as Admin or Agent.

    • Select a Routing profile, such as Basic Routing Profile.

    • Click Save.

2.2 Claim test phone number

Next, claim a temporary phone number and associate it with the sample inbound flow for testing.

To claim a test phone number

  1. Navigate to the Phone numbers page and click Claim a number:

  2. On the Claim Phone number page:

    • Select Voice as the channel if it isn't already selected by default.

    • Click the DID tab. Toll-free is also supported, but DIDs are cheaper for testing.

    • Select the country.

    • Select an available phone number from the list.

    • Select the Sample inbound flow (first contact experience) contact flow supplied by Amazon Connect.

    • Click Save.

2.3 Enable outbound dialing (Optional)

If outbound calling is part of your validation plan, assign the test number as the caller ID for the basic queue.

To enable outbound dialing

  1. To test outbound calling, navigate to the Queues page and click BasicQueue:

  2. On the Edit BasicQueue page, scroll down to Settings - optional.

  3. Search for and select the phone number you claimed in Step 2.2, then click Save.

Step 3: Test telephony capabilities

In this section, you'll verify federated access, then test inbound and outbound calling.

3.1 Test federated access to Amazon Connect and AWS

Verify that the Zendesk account provides the expected federated access to both Amazon Connect and the AWS Management Console.

To test federated access to Amazon Connect and AWS

  1. Log out of the AWS Management Console unless you're using an incognito browser tab.

  2. Log out of and back into your Zendesk account.

  3. Navigate to the Contact Center configuration console.

  4. From the Overview page:

    1. Click the Amazon Connect Dashboard link to validate federated access to the Amazon Connect Dashboard.

    2. Click the AWS Console link to verify access to the AWS Management Console.

For example:

3.2 Test inbound calling

Use the test number to place an inbound call, confirm that it reaches an available agent, and verify the resulting ticket data.

To test inbound calling

  1. From the Support page in Zendesk, click the user icon in the top-right corner and select Online to make the agent available:

  2. Call the phone number claimed in Step 2.2. Follow the menu options offered by Amazon Connect to be placed in a queue and transferred to an agent.

  3. Accept the incoming call and close the notification:

  4. Speak a few words to validate the recording and call transcription, then end the call.

  5. Click Finish wrap-up to close the Amazon Connect contact:

  6. Wait a few minutes to verify that the call recording and transcription are appended to the ticket. This may take up to four to five minutes:

3.3 Test outbound calling

After inbound calling is validated, place an outbound call to confirm that the agent calling workflow is configured correctly.

To test outbound calling

  1. From the Support page in Zendesk, click the phone icon. Enter a phone number and click Call:

  2. When the call is connected and your phone rings, click End to hang up.

  3. Click Finish wrap-up in the pop-up window to close the contact.

Step 4: Clean up (Optional)

When testing is complete, remove the temporary resources and test data that are no longer needed.

To clean up the test resources

  1. Clear the Outbound caller ID number from the BasicProfile routing profile in Amazon Connect.

  2. Release the phone number claimed in Step 2.2 because it was intended only for testing.

  3. Delete any tickets created in Zendesk during testing and validation.

articles.name: Overwrite Tags action fail to work on tickets
articles.title: Overwrite Tags action fail to work on tickets
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

The action Overwrite Tags does not work in Sunshine Conversations and my AI agent. Tags carry over from one ticket and conversation to the next. How do I avoid this situation? This issue confuses my reporting.

Resolution steps

Because the Overwrite action is set to replace tags with ai_agent_start_conversation at the Conversation started event, any session-specific tags added during the flow might remain on the conversation after that session ends.

To clear old tags, keep session tags, and control escalation routing:

  1. At conversation start, run Overwrite conversation tags with a space or blank first to clear inherited tags such as active_incident
  2. Immediately after or at the escalation point in the flow, run Add conversation tags to apply session-relevant tags such as bot_handled. This ensures only intentional tags are present from the start.
  3. If the issue persists, create a configured action using the Sunshine Conversations CRM target and set the task to Clear cached conversation. Add this action at the bot level and set it to trigger on the Session ended event, which fires when the conversation ends, an escalation attempt happens, or the conversation reaches the end of the session duration.
  4. If you expect an agent to use a macro to overwrite tags, ensure the custom role permission linked to the agent has Edit ticket tags enabled.

Following these steps ensures that:

  • Old tags do not bleed into new conversations, and bot_handled is set correctly for reporting and routing.
  • The escalation tag is applied only at the right moment, not inherited from a previous session.
  • You clear the conversation data saved in the session cache within AI agents and force a fresh retrieval of conversation fields at the start of the next session. Tags should not persist on the new ticket after the session ends.

articles.name: With AI agents, my API parameter doesn't store information
articles.title: With AI agents, my API parameter doesn't store information
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

With AI agents, my API parameter doesn't store information. The variable isn't stored, and it removes the variable. I use this procedure: Get Product Details [Dev]. The key 'product_detail' isn't saved, or it's overwritten with the product URL.

When running an API integration and setting a 'Key' or 'Parameter' via JSONata, is that stored automatically when using a procedure, or do I need to add it explicitly within the procedure to Collect parameter? Each time I try to collect the specific parameter to ensure it's stored, it creates an action to map to a new parameter. It doesn't set the parameter, even if the API runs successfully.

Resolution steps

No, a parameter isn't always stored automatically just because the API call succeeds. Request parameters send data to the API, but aren't stored for later steps.

To collect a parameter from an entity:

  1. Use Entity Recognized with your Customer Message blocks

  2. To use Entity Recognized as an input to an API call or within a conditional block further down the dialog, use Collect parameter and save that parameter under its name

For more information, see:

  • Managing generative procedures for AI agents

  • Creating dialogues to define scripted conversation flows for AI agents

articles.name: How can I disable or enable attachments in messaging?
articles.title: How can I disable or enable attachments in messaging?
articles.body:
Question

I don't want my customers or end users to be able to upload attachments and files into the AI agent. How can I disable or enable attachments in messaging? Can I turn off attachments?

Answer

Yes, you can control whether the attachment button appears in the composer from Admin Center.

To turn on or turn off attachments in messaging:

  1. In Admin Center, click Channels in the sidebar, then select Messaging and social > Messaging
  2. Click your Android channel
  3. Click the Style tab and scroll to the bottom
  4. Select the Allow customers to upload attachments option to turn it on, or uncheck it to turn it off
  5. Click Save

This setting immediately affects the visibility of the attachment button for your users.

See these articles for more information:

  • Allowing attachments in tickets
  • Configuring the widget frame
  • Supported file types for messaging attachments

articles.name: Zendesk certification FAQ
articles.title: Zendesk certification FAQ
articles.body:
Overview

A Zendesk certification is a professional credential that validates your expertise with Zendesk products and tools. It’s a valuable career achievement that helps you demonstrate job-ready skills, strengthen your professional profile, and pursue new opportunities in customer experience.

This article covers:

  • Certifications
  • Certification exam results and badges
  • Academy platform
  • Enrollment

Certifications

Can I retake a certification exam?

Yes. Each retake requires a new purchase at the current exam price.

How long is a Zendesk certification valid?

Zendesk certifications are valid for two years. After that, you must repurchase and retake the exam to recertify.

Are certification exams available in other languages?

Yes, some exams are available in other languages. Use the language filters in the certification catalog on Zendesk Academy to see the available options.

Certification exam results and badges

Why didn't I receive my certification exam results or badge?

Results and badges can take up to 72 hours to be issued after an exam. If you still do not see an update after 72 hours, contact academy@zendesk.com with your name, Academy email, and the exam you took.

Why did I receive an error after taking my certification exam?

In most cases, this means the proctoring system flagged the session for review. Contact academy@zendesk.com for further investigation.

I can't find my badge after passing a certification exam. How can I fix it?

If you are not seeing your badge after passing the exam, contact academy@zendesk.com.

Academy platform

I can't log in to my Academy account. What should I do?

The Academy login is different from your Zendesk login. Click Forgot password? in the sign in modal of the Academy and follow the instructions.

Can users host Zendesk Academy content on their own learning platform?

No, it’s not possible to host Zendesk Academy outside the Zendesk environment.

Can admins track their team's learning activity on Academy?

This is not available in a self-serve way. Work with your CSM or contact academy@zendesk.com for static updates.

Enrollment

My promo code isn't working. What should I do?

Contact academy@zendesk.com with the promo code. The team will check whether the code has expired, was already used, or applies only to a specific course or exam language.

Can I get a refund?

Refunds are reviewed on a case-by-case basis and not guaranteed. Email academy@zendesk.com with the reason for your request, and the team will guide you through the next steps.

articles.name: Customizing an AI agent’s opening and closing lines in email responses
articles.title: Customizing an AI agent’s opening and closing lines in email responses
articles.body:
You can customize opening and closing lines for your AI agent's email responses. The customized text is sent exactly as written. It isn't generated, translated, or modified by the AI agent, and it isn't affected by the AI agent'sinstructionsor otherpersonalization settings, including tone of voice or pronoun formality.

What's my plan?
All Suites Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus
Support Team, Professional, or Enterprise
This article applies only to email AI agents with agentic AI.

You can customize opening and closing lines for your AI agent's email responses. The customized text is sent exactly as written. It isn't generated, translated, or modified by the AI agent, and it isn't affected by the AI agent's instructions or other personalization settings, including tone of voice or pronoun formality.

If you don’t customize specific opening and closing lines, the AI agent uses AI-generated text for its openings and closings.

This article contains the following topics:

  • Customizing an AI agent’s opening and closing lines
  • Using AI-generated opening and closing lines

Customizing an AI agent’s opening and closing lines

You can customize the opening and closing lines of email responses by creating templates for each language you support.

Keep the following limitations in mind:

  • The email footer remains static and can't be edited.
  • Templates aren't translated automatically. You provide your own version of each template for every language you support.
  • Templates are fixed strings. The AI agent doesn't adjust their grammar, so languages with gender- or case-sensitive forms (such as the vocative case in Polish) may need wording that avoids inflected names.

To customize an AI agent's email opening and closing lines

  1. In the AI agents workspace, select the AI agent you want to work with.
  2. Click Content in the sidebar, then select Email content.
  3. Click Manage languages in the upper-right to select one of the supported languages you’ve added.
  4. Click Opening line and enter the text the AI agent should use at the beginning of each email response.

    Optionally, you can personalize the text with the customer’s name. Place the cursor where you want to insert the name, type a forward slash (/), and select one of the following options:

    • customerFirstName
    • customerLastName
    • customerFullName

    Note: If your AI agent was created before July 30, 2026, see Populating the customer name variables for an additional step required to use the customer name variables listed above.
    Alternatively, leave the field empty to use an AI-generated opening line.
  5. Click Closing line and enter the text the AI agent should use at the end of each email response.

    Optionally, you can personalize the text with the customer’s name, as described above.

    Alternatively, leave the field empty to use an AI-generated opening line.
  6. Click Save.
  7. In the Languages panel, click the options menu () for the language you’re customizing and select Enable.

Using AI-generated opening and closing lines

You can configure your AI agent to use AI-generated opening and closing lines, instead of specifically customized ones.

You can do this by leaving the fields blank when you customize the opening and closing lines, or by disabling opening and closing line customizations for a language altogether.

You can disable customizations for a language only if you’ve previously enabled them.

To disable opening and closing customizations

  1. In the AI agents workspace, select the AI agent you want to work with.
  2. Click Content in the sidebar, then select Email content.
  3. Click Manage languages in the upper-right to select one of the supported languages you’ve added.
  4. Click the options menu () for the language you want to disable opening and closing customizations for, then select Disable.

articles.title: Release notes through 2026-08-21
articles.body:
See the What's New section for an overview of what was released last month.

This week's release notes include:

  • Knowledge and AI agents
  • Voice
  • Zendesk Workforce Management (WFM)
  • Apps and integrations
  • Products with no updates this week

Knowledge and AI agents

Editor

Fixed: 

  • Signing out while viewing a different brand's Help Center (via ?brand_id=…) sent users to /hc on the default brand, 404ing if that brand had no HC; GuideChromeController#sign_out_path now uses the brand actually being rendered. 
  • The SSRF guard added previously blocked trusted, server-generated download URLs from the Asset Upload Service that legitimately resolve to cluster-local addresses; those AUS-derived call sites now skip destination verification. 
  • Fixed translation routing losing the locale after switching translations. Switching to the HTML body for translations stopped returning a locale, breaking translation routing updates. 
  • Removing a callout with the caret inside it could leave the accordion's content without a paragraph; callout removal now uses CKEditor's native widget deletion so an empty, editable paragraph is restored.
  • Preview surfaces (HTML preview, AI translation modal, diff views) weren't loading the shared baseline CSS, causing unstyled or double-styled callouts against the editor's own callout.css.
  • Inserting content after (or around) a tabs or accordion component was not possible when it was the last element. Pressing escape now focuses the block so content can be added above or below.

Voice

New: 

  • Agents can now collapse the live call transcript and call summary panels in Voice, making it easier to focus on the active call while keeping those details available when needed. See Using generative AI to create call summaries and transcripts on tickets.

Question

With an agentic email bot, the procedure contains several parameters to collect from an API request. In one conversation, I asked to connect directly to an agent. However, the bot prompted the end user to set parameter values, which isn't ideal. How can I fix this?

Answer

Content entities are the easiest way to collect these parameters from the initial email text.

To fix this:

  • Ensure that these session parameters are captured, using entities, actions, or API integrations

  • Edit the procedure to ensure that these don't use Collect Parameters blocks to check for parameters that should already exist. It's best to use Check Condition blocks.

articles.name: Why can’t I find tickets when searching a numeric custom field with a very large value?
articles.title: Why can’t I find tickets when searching a numeric custom field with a very large value?
articles.body:
Question

Why search does not return expected results when I search using a very large value in a numeric custom ticket field?

Answer

Zendesk search supports numeric custom field values only within the following range:

  • -9,223,372,036,854,775,808 to 9,223,372,036,854,775,807

If a numeric field contains a value outside this range, search for that value may not return expected ticket results.

This limit is a numeric value limit, not a character limit. This behavior is due to a limitation of the search backend.

For example, if you need to store and search identifiers larger than this range, consider a text field instead of a numeric field.

Use numeric fields for values that fit within the supported 64-bit signed integer range. Use text fields for very large numeric identifiers that you must search.

To learn more about searching for tickets, see Searching Zendesk Support data.

articles.name: Understanding advanced action flows (EAP)
articles.title: Understanding advanced action flows (EAP)
articles.body:
Advanced action flows provide a more powerful way to build automation for service by supporting workflows that can branch, pause for human input, connect across systems, and adapt as business rules evolve. This allows teams to automate more of their work, reducing manual effort and increasing scalability and control.

What's my plan?
All Suites Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus

Summary: ◀▼

Advanced action flows let you automate complex, long-running workflows with branching, pauses, and integrations across many systems using code. They support custom API calls, detailed error tracking, version control, and reuse across workflows. Use them for workflows needing complex logic, human approvals, or attachment processing. They run in secure sandboxes with execution limits and require authentication for external APIs.

Advanced action flows provide a more powerful way to build automation for service by supporting workflows that can branch, pause for human input, connect across systems, and adapt as business rules evolve. This allows teams to automate more of their work, reducing manual effort and increasing scalability and control.

This article contains the following topics:
  • Understanding the difference between action flows and advanced action flows
  • Choosing the best automated workflow for your use cases
  • Essential facts about advanced action flows
Related articles
  • Creating advanced action flows
  • Advanced action flows API reference
  • Editing and managing advanced action flows
  • Monitoring and troubleshooting advanced action flows

Understanding the difference between action flows and advanced action flows

Action flows and advanced action flows both address the same class of use case: automated sequences of steps that can perform actions in Zendesk and external systems. In general, action flows are best for no or low-code repeatable automated workflows that are simple or moderately complex, while advanced action flows are code-based and designed for more complex and variable workflows.

The following table provides an in-depth comparison of action flows and advanced action flows:
  Action flows Advanced action flows
Creation method Drag-and-drop components in visual builder Conversational AI prompt that generates editable code
Visual diagram Built by the user in the action builder Generated based on the code
Complexity Low to medium complexity workflows Low to high complexity workflows
Automation style Structured, repeatable process automation Flexible orchestration to support complex business logic
Extending to new APIs Must be predefined as an action All REST APIs supported
Troubleshooting, drafts, and version control Visual review, testing, and step-based editing. Direct access to code, execution traces, and version history, including visual review of the generated flowchart.
Typical user Admins and process owners who prefer not to write code Technical admins, developers, and process owners
Ownership model Better for broad admin adoption and ease of use Better for precision and control

Choosing the best automated workflow for your use cases

Because action flows and advanced action flows have overlapping capabilities, it's important to understand when they can both accomplish your goals and when one is a better choice over the other.

When to use advanced action flows

Advanced action flows are typically the best choice if your workflow requires:
  • Long-running processes over days or weeks, often with human approval steps in the middle.
  • Complex business logic, such as nested conditions, loops, regular expressions, parsing JSON or custom objects, handling exceptions, or sharing states across steps.
  • Attachment processing, such as reading data out of invoices, IDs, spreadsheets, or archives.
  • Integrations with many systems, particularly internal, legacy, or niche APIs that aren't supported as pre-built connectors for action builder.

Examples that are well-suited to advanced action flows include: dynamic API calls, advanced data transformations, multi-branching logic, and retries.

Other benefits of advanced action flows include:
  • Unlike action flows, you aren't limited to pre-built connectors. Instead, you can use new, internal, or legacy REST API endpoints immediately without having to manually create custom actions. Additionally, every endpoint and parameter the service supports is available for use in your advanced action flows, including endpoints released after your workflow is created.
  • Because advanced action flows call APIs directly, you don't have to maintain connectors.
  • Every time you save an advanced action flow, a version is saved in the version history, making it easy to track changes and revert to an earlier version if necessary. Each advanced action flow has a currently published version as well as read-only snapshots of all prior versions.
  • Every time an advanced action flow runs, every execution records console outputs, network requests and responses, inputs, outputs, and errors. This information makes it possible to quickly identify the problem if failures occur.
  • Advanced action flows have predictable behavior and cost at scale, consuming neither action credits nor model tokens unless you add an AI step.
  • Advanced action flows can be invoked by AI agents and other workflows, making them reusable across the Zendesk platform.
It's also important to understand what you can't do with advanced action flows. You can't:
  • Install or import third-party packages
  • Access the system
  • Open raw sockets
  • Use the following JavaScript features: eval, Proxy, Reflect, WeakMap, WeakSet, WeakRef, SharedArrayBuffer, and WebAssembly
  • Rely on variables after the workflow is paused

If advanced action flows are a good fit for your workflow, see Creating advanced action flows.

When to use action flows

Action flows are typically the best choice if your workflow requires:
  • No code or low-code workflow creation and management.
  • Lower complexity logic for the workflow.
  • Highly repeatable and structured steps that are defined with the supported Zendesk steps and pre-built connector steps.

Examples that are well-suited to action flows include: ticket routing, approvals, status updates, and other standard workflow automations.

For more information, see Creating action flows to automate processes across Zendesk and external systems.

Essential facts about advanced action flows

Consider the following key concepts and details before creating advanced action flows:
  • Advanced action flows consist of the following parts:
    1. Advanced action flow trigger: The condition under which the workflow is initiated. This could be a Zendesk event (ticket, user, organization, asset, or custom object is created, updated, or deleted), a recurring schedule, manual initiation, a webhook called by an external system, or invocation by an AI agent or other workflow.
    2. Actions: Each action is an annotated section of your code that appears as a node in the flowchart and as a boundary in the execution interface.

      Steps can include a Pause, which causes the workflow to stop and wait for a specified duration of time, an event to occur, an approval to be received, or for another workflow to finish.

  • Generally speaking, advanced action flows use AI during the workflow creation process to generate the code and a flowchart, but not when the workflow itself is running.

    However, it is possible to incorporate AI actions into the workflow, in which case AI is used for that process as well. To incorporate AI into your advanced action flows, use the agents.run() call.

  • Advanced action flows run in isolated environments with platform globals instead of Node.js or browser APIs. The isolated environment is referred to as a sandbox. This means there is no file system, raw sockets, or packages to import.
    Each capability your workflow uses, whether that's making an HTTP request, reading a ticket, or storing a value, is a request to the host platform, which validates the request before acting. Several isolation layers sit between your code and Zendesk infrastructure, including separate runner processes, dedicated virtual machine instance per execution with its own memory ceiling, a container with no network egress permitted, and a read-only file system running as a non-privileged user. Because of these precautions, advanced action flows can't reach anything they haven't been explicitly granted access to and can't affect the data or workflows of other accounts.
    Note: The sandboxes used to isolate the advanced action flows are not the same as Zendesk sandboxes, which are used by admins and agents with permission to test features and configurations outside of their production environment.
  • All API calls made by an advanced action flow are attributed to the administrator who created the workflow. This means the workflow has the same permissions and access as the creator and are constrained by your account's normal rate limits. In the code, user.creator identifies the workflow's author and user.runner identifies the user or system that triggered the latest execution.
  • When defining an advanced action flow that calls APIs in external systems, you must authenticate the connection as required by the system. This could be through a registered OAuth connection or providing an API key or bearer token that is stored as an encrypted Secret within the workflow. It is also possible to use APIs that have no authentication requirements.
  • Zendesk API access is deny-by-default against an allowlist. Advanced action flows run with the permissions and account rate limits associated with the admin who created the workflow.
  • Local variables don't persist through pause steps in advanced action flows. Any variables needed after a pause step must be in storage.

Understanding advanced action flow limits

The following execution limits are enforced by Zendesk. Exceeding these limits results in runtime errors that are recorded in the execution trace.

Execution limits

Limit Value
Execution timeout Default of 5 minutes, but can be configured between 1 second and 10 minutes.

pause() isn't counted aggainst the execution timeout, but sleep() is counted.
Memory 128 MB per execution
Maximum pause duration 30 days
Concurrent HTTP requests within one execution 8
Concurrent AI steps within one execution 4
Recorded operations per execution 100,000
Automatic retries on failed requests Up to 5 for server errors and rate-limit responses

Data size limits

Limit Value
Flow output 2 MB
HTTP request body 48 MB
agent.run() text input 20 KiB
Rows per parse operation (CSV, TSV, XLSX) 10,000
Storage value 4 KB
Storage keys per scope 1,000
Storage key length 255 characters
Flow code size 512 KB

articles.name: How can I add a hyperlink or image to my signature?
articles.title: How can I add a hyperlink or image to my signature?
articles.body:
Question

How do I customize my signature with hyperlinks and images? Can I use a locally saved image in my signature?

Answer

No. You can't use an image saved locally on your computer in your agent signature.

To use an image in your signature, upload the file to a public image hosting site or save it as an asset in your knowledge base. This process generates a public URL that you can use in the Markdown code for your signature.

You can use Markdown formatting to add images and hyperlinks to your signature.

To add a hyperlink in Support:

  1. Click your avatar at the top right corner and then select Manage profile. 

  2. Under Signature on the left-hand panel, type the Markdown text below.

    [Link display text]
(https://www.zendesk.com)


Alternatively, add an image that is also a link using this Markdown:

[![alttext](imageurl)](linkurl)
  • Replace linkurl with the link for the image to direct toward
  • Replace imageurl with the link to the hosted image. After you resize the image, use an image host such as imgur.com > Wait five seconds for the image to load > Right-click the image > Select Copy image link. This returns the link to paste instead of imageurl

To display the image without a clickable link, use this Markdown:

![](imageurl)

This functionality also applies to global and brand signatures.

Tip: Use a PNG or JPEG file and size the image to a smaller size, between 5 KB to 50 KB. For optimal display, start with an image size of approximately 120px wide by 40px high. Adjust as needed to maintain the logo proportions. Ensure the image is on an HTTPS server and test the signature in email clients and the Agent Workspace to ensure proper display.

articles.name: A conversation displays an automated resolution but it was escalated to an agent
articles.title: A conversation displays an automated resolution but it was escalated to an agent
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

A conversation in an email escalated to an agent, but it shows an automated resolution. An escalation shouldn’t be an automated resolution. What happened?

Resolution steps

From your description of the behavior, the conversation isn’t an email interaction. It’s a messaging conversation, handled by the AI agent.

The AI agent attempted to escalate the conversation to a human agent, but no agents were available to accept the handoff. For this reason, the escalation couldn't complete. Instead, the bot created a ticket for follow-up and then finished the conversation itself.

This explains why you see both elements:

  • Custom resolution: Escalated to agent — because the bot reached the escalation step and attempted the handoff
  • Conversation status: Automated resolution — because no human agent actually joined the live messaging conversation, so it ended with the bot

While labels can look contradictory at first, labels describe two different parts of the same flow. In this case, it appears to be a failed handoff or no-agents-available scenario in messaging, rather than an email case or a successful live escalation to an agent.

articles.name: Can I prioritize the use case resolution with AI agents and emails?
articles.title: Can I prioritize the use case resolution with AI agents and emails?
articles.body:
Question

With a double intent in emails with an AI agent, can we prioritize the order of my use case resolutions?

Answer

No, there isn't a way to prioritize the resolution with more than one or multiple use cases.

  • The AI agent will try to solve as many use cases as your settings allow.
  • In addition, the AI agent will only start the next use case if the customer asks for it.
